title: HTML Can Do That
author: encyclopedism
relevanceReason: 命中 2 个 AI/科技关键词。
summaryRaw: HTML has been gobbling up swathes of what used to be JavaScript’s remit. This page lists a bunch of dynamic functionality that we can now achieve with just HTML.

Update 2026-08-20: I originally built this page in one hour during HTML Day 2026 to write and celebrate HTML, but I’ve since made some edits to better express and highlight where the browser implementation of some of this stuff is severely lacking and/or completely fails to meet accessibility needs. So, by all means, try it out, but make it as accessible as you can!

popover Browser Support: popover → Light dismiss, Esc to close, no managing z-index to wrangle it onto a top layer. All managed with popover and popovertarget (and popovertargetaction) attributes in HTML. (MDN) No JavaScript, just modern browser magic, thanks to the wonderful folks speccing for the web and building our browsers!

No JavaScript, just modern browser magic, thanks to the wonderful folks speccing for the web and building our browsers!

Browser Support: dialog → Similar thing going on as popover here, except this time with a dedicated element for modal dialog boxes. (MDN) See command / commandFor below for another, more recently-landing feature that allows us to open and close dialog elements (and will be useful for lots of other non-JS functionality, one day!). Once again the popover attribute is doing some heavy-lifting here!

Closed with just HTML via <form method="dialog">, opened with the popover attribute.

Even though it’s sort of against the spirit of this page, I want to include this short snippet of how to interact with dialog elements in JavaScript: This one is opened with .showModal() and closed with .close(), both called from JavaScript. Show JS-powered dialog code

This one is opened with .showModal() and closed with .close(), both called from JavaScript.

 document.getElementById("example-dialog-js-open").addEventListener("click", () => { document.getElementById("example-dialog-js").showModal() }) document.getElementById("example-dialog-js-close").addEventListener("click", () => { document.getElementById("example-dialog-js").close() })

comments.author: dajonker
comments.textRawHtml:
Popover, dialog, invoker commands, our entire production app uses these everywhere and it works really well! The fact that dialogs and popovers are rendered on the "top layer" and that nested popovers are also automatically stacked on top of each other and have 'cascading close' shows how well these standards were designed.

The only hard thing is still to position a popover near the element that triggers it, such as when you want to create a context menu that has to render above/below the button that triggered it. There is anchor positioning in CSS now but support is still limited and I find it hard to wrap my head around.

LLMs are also terrible at these new standards. If they even know about them, they often think they're not baseline yet and they have almost zero training data compared to the giant mountain of weird JS and CSS that people had to use before the introduction of these standards.
comments.textZhHtml:
弹出窗口、对话框、调用器命令，我们的整个生产应用程序到处都使用这些，而且效果非常好！事实上，对话框和弹出框是在“顶层”呈现的，嵌套弹出框也会自动堆叠在彼此之上并具有“级联关闭”，这表明这些标准的设计有多好。

唯一困难的事情仍然是将弹出框放置在触发它的元素附近，例如当您想要创建一个必须在触发它的按钮上方/下方呈现的上下文菜单时。 CSS 现在已经有了锚点定位，但支持仍然有限，我发现很难理解。

法学硕士在这些新标准上也很糟糕。如果他们甚至了解它们，他们通常会认为它们还不是基线，与人们在引入这些标准之前必须使用的怪异 JS 和 CSS 的巨山相比，它们的训练数据几乎为零。

children.author: alwillis
children.textRawHtml:
> LLMs are also terrible at these new standards. If they even know about them, they often think they're not baseline yet…

It doesn’t have to be that way.

You could create a Skill [1] that tells the agent to use modern css; the newer models like Opus 5 are probably much better with modern css.

Google released a set of skills at I/O called Modern Web Guidance [2] that steer coding agents to use modern css and best practices.

[1]: https://www.skills.sh/paulirish/dotfiles/modern-css

[2]: https://developer.chrome.com/docs/modern-web-guidance/get-st...
children.textZhHtml:
> 法学硕士在这些新标准上也很糟糕。如果他们甚至了解它们，他们通常会认为自己还没有达到基线......

不一定是这样。

您可以创建一个技能 [1] 告诉代理使用现代 CSS；像 Opus 5 这样的新模型在使用现代 CSS 时可能会更好。

Google 在 I/O 上发布了一套名为“现代 Web 指导”[2] 的技能，引导编码代理使用现代 CSS 和最佳实践。

[1]: https://www.skills.sh/paulirish/dotfiles/modern-css

[2]: https://developer.chrome.com/docs/modern-web-guidance/get-st...

children.author: chmod775
children.textRawHtml:
Can we stop calling them skills? They're mostly just documents like any other. Call them cheat-sheets or guides.

Wrapping an .md file in all this circus, with lingo carefully designed to hide the fact that under the hood you're really just dumping another text file into the LLM's context , helps nobody but people's AI psychosis.

But I guess "my LLM can use skills" sounds a lot cooler than "my LLM can read text files", so we'd rather keep pretending really hard.
children.textZhHtml:
我们可以停止称它们为技能吗？它们大多只是像其他文件一样的文件。称它们为备忘单或指南。

在所有这些马戏团中包装一个 .md 文件，用精心设计的行话来隐藏这样一个事实，即在幕后你实际上只是将另一个文本文件转储到 LLM 的上下文中，除了人们的 AI 精神病之外没有帮助任何人。

但我想“我的 LLM 可以使用技能”听起来比“我的 LLM 可以读取文本文件”酷得多，所以我们宁愿继续假装真的很难。

children.author: doginasuit
children.textRawHtml:
> The only hard thing is still to position a popover near the element that triggers it, such as when you want to create a context menu that has to render above/below the button that triggered it.

If you put something like this in your popover class, it will resolve to the button that called it when position-anchor is not set:

top: anchor(bottom);

I'm not sure how widely supported it is but I've been using it in Firefox/Chrome.
children.textZhHtml:
> 唯一困难的事情仍然是将弹出框放置在触发它的元素附近，例如当您想要创建一个必须在触发它的按钮上方/下方呈现的上下文菜单时。

如果您在弹出框类中放置类似的内容，它将解析为在未设置位置锚点时调用它的按钮：

top:anchor(bottom);

我不确定支持的范围有多大是的，但我一直在 Firefox/Chrome 中使用它。

children.author: extra88
children.textRawHtml: All current browsers support anchor positioning including popover buttons being the implicit anchor. However, the anchor positioning polyfill does not support this, it requires an explicit anchor-name.
children.textZhHtml: 所有当前浏览器都支持锚点定位，包括作为隐式锚点的弹出按钮。然而，锚点定位polyfill不支持这一点，它需要一个显式的锚点名称。

children.author: sublinear
children.textRawHtml:
I'm curious how many people are involved in the design of your app and what their concerns are.

Testing for accessibility and on mobile devices has a tendency to derail the best intentions. What tools are you using for those concerns? I'm not asking because I need advice. I'm asking because I want to know what you or your team did.
children.textZhHtml:
我很好奇有多少人参与了您的应用的设计以及他们关心的是什么。

在移动设备上进行可访问性测试往往会偏离最佳意图。您使用什么工具来解决这些问题？我问这个问题并不是因为我需要建议。我问这个问题是因为我想知道您或您的团队做了什么。

children.author: dajonker
children.textRawHtml:
It's a small team of four, everyone works on the "full stack" which is Rails with HTMX and very little JS. As the lead dev, I am usually the one to make the decision that we should use the modern browser standards.

It's a niche B2B SaaS app and luckily we know most of our users personally. They all use modern browsers, usually Chrome or Edge on Windows. There is not a lot of mobile usage although we do support it.

children.author: sublinear
children.textRawHtml:
Yes. The maintenance costs of these models are very high. Something's gotta give soon.

It's exactly like trying to acquire a bootleg of a movie, but all you can afford is a single blurry jpeg taken from the back row of a theater.

What's worse is you're an alien who wants to understand life on Earth by watching this single movie. That's how far away we are from AGI.
children.textZhHtml:
是的。这些型号的维护成本非常高。有些东西必须尽快放弃。

这就像试图购买盗版电影一样，但你所能承担的只是从剧院后排拍摄的一张模糊的 jpeg。

更糟糕的是，你是一个外星人，想通过观看这一部电影来了解地球上的生活。这就是我们离通用人工智能有多远。
